context: WebGL particle flow simulation with 200K particles tracing a synthetic curl-noise vector field, colored by velocity magnitude from indigo (slow) to yellow (fast), with a legend and interactive controls for count and speed.
first_impression: A visually honest WebGL animation demo where color correctly encodes velocity magnitude via linear interpolation, though D3 is barely used and the encoding is largely aesthetic rather than data-representational.
what_works: Velocity-to-color mapping uses correct linear interpolation of magnitude (sqrt of vx²+vy²) with a labeled slow-to-fast legend; particle alpha fades at end-of-life transparently and does not encode data deceptively.
what_doesnt: Velocity normalization uses a hardcoded magic number (mag/1.1) that will silently clip particles above that threshold to the same max color, breaking the color encoding for any data where the field magnitude exceeds 1.1; the subset relation is mildly brittle since reducing particle count mid-stream leaves stale GPU buffer data for the inactive tail.
